title: Shepherds who feed themselves (Ezekiel 34)
hook: leaders who fleece the flock; God will seek the lost and bind the broken

segments.voice: Yesterday, the watchman on the wall: see the danger, blow the trumpet, and leave the choice to them. Your line was the watchman warns. Did you say your one sentence? Day eight hundred twelve.

It's the end of a week, so look back. A covenant written on the heart. A field bought in a city under siege, the deed sealed in a jar. A scroll cut into the fire and written again, longer. Then we crossed from Jeremiah to Ezekiel: a throne with wheels by a river in Babylon, a scroll that tasted like honey, a watchman on a wall. Prophets speaking to people who have lost almost everything. And today Ezekiel turns from the people to the people in charge. The leaders of Israel are called shepherds, and he has a question for them.
screen: `A WEEK OF TWO PROPHETS.` → `FIELD, SCROLL, WHEELS, HONEY, WALL.` → `NOW, THE SHEPHERDS.`

segments.voice: The question is blunt. In the King James words: "Woe be to the shepherds of Israel that do feed themselves! should not the shepherds feed the flocks?" Then the charges, one by one. You eat the fat and wear the wool. You kill the well-fed ones. But the weak you have not strengthened. The sick you have not healed. The broken you have not bound up. The ones driven away you have not brought back. The lost you have not looked for. Instead, the text says, you ruled them with force and with harshness. So the sheep scattered, and became food for wild animals, and no one went looking for them. Listen to that list again. It isn't about grand crimes. It's about neglect: a leader who takes what the job gives and skips what the job asks. Then the chapter turns, and God says, in effect: then I will do it myself. "I will seek that which was lost, and bring again that which was driven away, and will bind up that which was broken, and will strengthen that which was sick." Almost every failure on the first list is answered by a promise on the second. The text even talks about judging between sheep and sheep: the strong ones who push with shoulder and horn and muddy the water the others have to drink. The Bible says that Moses and David both kept sheep before they led anyone. A midrash tells that Moses was chosen after he followed one runaway young goat to a pool of water and carried it back on his shoulders. The picture of a leader in this chapter is someone who goes looking for the one who wandered off.
screen: `SHOULD NOT THE SHEPHERDS FEED THE FLOCK?` · `THE WEAK, THE SICK, THE BROKEN, THE LOST.` · then, large: `I WILL SEEK THAT WHICH WAS LOST.` · then: `MOSES AND THE RUNAWAY GOAT.`

segments.voice: Here's the practice: lead by serving. You may shepherd someone already: a kid, a team, a younger sibling, an aging parent, a friend who leans on you, a group chat you started. Settle, and breathe. Pick one flock that's yours. Then go down Ezekiel's list slowly. Who's weak? Who's sick? Who's been hurt? Who has drifted away? Let one face come. Don't fix anything yet. Just hold that person, the way a shepherd might carry a stray back. If you pray, you can pray for them by name. The bell holds the time.
shepherds, the leaders Ezekiel accuses of feeding themselves while the flock goes hungry, sick, and lost. Today's word.
Your line: seek the lost. Today, reach out to the one who drifted away from your flock: a message, a call, a seat saved for them. Day eight hundred twelve.

howItsDone: Jews read Ezekiel 34 among the Latter Prophets, and the image of the leader as shepherd is taught through the stories of Moses and David caring for their flocks.

myth: Ezekiel's charge is mostly about neglect
the weak, the sick, the broken, the driven away and the lost were left uncared for.
the chapter ends with the sheep left scattered
God promises to seek the lost and bind up the broken.
the chapter only judges the shepherds

fork.setup: the shepherds have fed themselves and let the flock scatter. what does the chapter say happens next?
options: the flock is left to fend for itself.
new shepherds are hired from abroad.
God says: I will seek the lost myself.
fork.reveal: God takes up the work the shepherds skipped: seek the lost, bring back the driven away, bind up the broken, strengthen the sick.

original.note: Hebrew: shepherd, the word Ezekiel uses for the leaders of Israel.

trapdoor: what you thought: a chapter about sheep farming.
what it means: a charge against leaders who take from the people and neglect them.
what a scholar hears: the failures on the shepherds' list are answered, almost point by point, by God's promise to do the work himself.
